guide.summary: Silla temples, tombs, museums and parks, with hotel breakfasts, dinners, bakeries and a bar checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Gyeongju Donggungwon closes on Mondays and Gyeongju National Museum closes on the second Monday of March, June, September and December, so a Monday suits Bulguksa Temple, which its own site says is open year-round.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Gyeongju Donggungwon closes on Mondays (the next weekday when Monday is a public holiday), 1 January and the Seollal and Chuseok days. Gyeongju National Museum closes on 1 January, Seollal and Chuseok, and on the second Monday of March, June, September and December.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: Bulguksa Temple's site says admission has been free since 4 May 2023. Gyeongju City's admission page lists Cheomseongdae as free and Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond and Cheonmachong at 3,000 won for adults.

toolkit.label: Booking
toolkit.copy: Kolon Hotel Gyeongju says the Yeonhyangsang set at The Hangonggan and its Judabyeol Bangwa snack set must be booked in advance. Its Kids Chef Pizza Lab runs from 14:00 with online booking.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Bulguksa Temple's visiting page says pets may not enter. Gyeongju Donggungwon also bars pets, smoking and drones, and allows outside food only in designated outdoor areas.

guide.dek: Pair Bulguksa Temple with Seokguram Grotto, keep Mondays away from Donggungwon, and check the museum's second-Monday closures before you fix dates.
intro: Bulguksa Temple, at 385 Bulguk-ro, anchors the eastern side of Gyeongju. Its own visiting page says admission has been free since 4 May 2023 under the revised heritage law, that pets may not enter, and that parking costs 2,000 won for a car. That page carries no update date; it lists last entry at 17:00 from November to January. A notice on the temple's board says repairs to the Daeungjeon main hall do not affect entry. Up the mountain, Seokguram Grotto at 238 Seokgul-ro posts 2026 prayer notices, but its hours page could not be read.

In the centre, Gyeongju National Museum at 186 Iljeong-ro lists hours of 10:00 to 18:00, with last entry 30 minutes before closing and Saturday evenings to 20:00 from March to October. It closes on 1 January, Seollal and Chuseok, and on the second Monday of March, June, September and December. A lobby display reuniting two stone-tablet fragments from Wolseong runs until 31 December 2026. The museum's Children's Museum has been closed since 1 July 2025 until further notice.

Gyeongju City's admission page lists Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond and the Cheonmachong tomb in Daereungwon at 3,000 won for adults, while Cheomseongdae is free and shares the Daereungwon car park. A city walking route following King Munmu begins at Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond and continues to the Wolseong fortress site. Gyochon Hanok Village sits at 39-2 Gyochon-gil. Out at Bomun, Gyeongju Donggungwon opens 09:30 to 19:00 with entry until 18:00, closes on Mondays, and does not allow pets or drones.

Gyeongju APEC Memorial Park, the renamed Expo park at 614 Gyeonggam-ro, lists park hours of 10:00 to 22:00 and exhibition halls to 18:00; its Solgeo Art Museum shows work by 권정순 from 3 October 2026 to 7 March 2027. For meals, Kolon Hotel Gyeongju lists The Chanran breakfast buffet at 07:00 to 10:00, Korean dishes at The Hangonggan, wood-fired pizza and the Moonlight Pocha chicken-and-beer bar. Kensington Resort Gyeongju lists a morning buffet, Ohas Bakery & Cafe, Ashley Queens and a garden barbecue, and Hwangnam-ppang's main store lists 08:00 to 22:00 daily.
summaryCards: Pair Bulguksa Temple and Seokguram Grotto in the east with Gyeongju National Museum, Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond and Cheomseongdae in the old centre.
Kolon Hotel Gyeongju lists The Chanran breakfast buffet at 07:00 to 10:00, and Hwangnam-ppang's main store lists 08:00 to 22:00 every day of the year.
Gyeongju Donggungwon closes on Mondays, and Gyeongju National Museum closes on the second Monday of March, June, September and December as well as 1 January, Seollal and Chuseok.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Only 22 places could be confirmed: many Gyeongju restaurants and cafés publish only on maps or social media, so food listings lean on hotel outlets at Kolon Hotel Gyeongju and Kensington Resort Gyeongju, and no cocktail bar could be confirmed (Moonlight Pocha is a chicken and draft-beer bar). Bulguksa Temple's hours come from an undated page; Seokguram Grotto's hours page returned an error; Gyeongju City pages give no hours for Donggung Palace and Wolji Pond, Daereungwon, Cheomseongdae, Wolseong or Gyochon, and their operating evidence is limited to current admission and 2026 route or event pages. Hours were not published for Olon Bakery Cafe or the Kensington outlets. Hilton Gyeongju (HTTP 403), Gyeongju Bird Park (certificate error), Lahan Select Gyeongju, Gyeongju World, Silla Millennium Park, Hanwha Resort Gyeongju, Yosokkoong, The-K Hotel Gyeongju and Gyeongju Arts Center could not be read.
